description: Hi! I'm an AI/ML Engineer and 4th-year Artificial Intelligence student from Uzbekistan. I have experience building machine learning models, AI agents, data analysis systems, and intelligent automation solutions. I'm interested in applying AI, satellite data, and geospatial technologies to solve real-world challenges. I'm looking for motivated teammates with skills in Python, Data Science, GIS, Remote Sensing, Computer Vision, and Frontend/UI design. Let's build something impactful together!
details:
What it does

TerraVision has one shared analysis core with modules on top of it.

Core analysis for any field:

  • climate history (NASA POWER): frost dates, heat days, drought index (SPI), FAO-56 evapotranspiration;
  • field history: what was grown each year, from Sentinel-2 NDVI phenology;
  • salinity level and trend;
  • soil properties (SoilGrids) and soil moisture (SMAP);
  • terrain (SRTM);
  • 7-day and ECMWF SEAS5 seasonal forecasts.

🌾 Crop module (the challenge core):

  • compares the current rotation with 3+ alternatives on water, income, soil health, salinity tolerance, climate risk and labour, weighted by the farmer's own priorities;
  • agronomic rules: frost-free season fit, FAO-29 salt tolerance, water limits, rotation breaks (for example, cotton monoculture and Verticillium wilt), legume benefits and bare summer fields;
  • a robustness score across normal, dry and hot years;
  • "what-if" sliders for rainfall and temperature;
  • every recommendation has a 5-part explanation: why, evidence, benefits, information gaps and risks.

🐄 Livestock module:

  • pasture greenness compared with a 20-year norm (MODIS);
  • estimated grazing capacity (MODIS NPP);
  • heat stress for animals (THI);
  • distance to water sources;
  • rotational grazing advice.

📍 Land selection: compares 2–4 plots for a chosen purpose, including FAO GAEZ suitability.

Additional features:

  • Work calendar with winter salt-leaching plans placed in periods when the soil is not frozen, with sowing dates based on soil temperature, and .ics export;
  • Actual vs. needed water use (Sentinel-2-based ET, checked against WaPOR and ECOSTRESS);
  • Seasonal water-supply signal from mountain snow cover (MODIS), river discharge (GloFAS) and groundwater (GRACE);
  • One-page Land Passport (PDF) for leasing, credit and contracts;
  • Simple and Expert modes, Uzbek in Latin and Cyrillic scripts, and NASA GIBS map layers.

Benefits and impact

TerraVision helps users:

  • use the bare months after the wheat harvest for a second crop;
  • choose salt-tolerant crops;
  • avoid over-irrigation;
  • plan winter leaching;
  • prepare for low-water years before sowing.

It is free, works in Uzbek and is designed for users with little technical background.

Tools and technologies

  • Backend: Python, FastAPI, pandas, NumPy, SciPy, pyet, Google Earth Engine API.
    • NASA Harvest's Presto model, fine-tuned on 8,435 labelled Uzbek field samples (Remelgado et al., 2020) for crop history (in development);
    • an LLM layer that explains results in plain Uzbek, with automatic number checking so it cannot invent figures (in development);
    • Claude was used as a coding and research assistant.

Creativity

  • One analysis core serves several user groups.
  • Strategies are ranked by robustness in bad years, not by a single "optimal" year.
  • Missing data is shown as "unknown", never as zero, and every number shows its source.
  • The tool produces locally practical outputs: a salt-leaching schedule that avoids frozen soil and a snow-based early warning for summer water supply.

Factors considered

  • Uzbekistan's cotton–wheat system, salinity and limited water.
    • ET0 checked against FAO-56 worked example 18 and ERA5;
    • phenology rules checked on real Sirdaryo fields;
    • planned: backtesting (2020 → 2021) and comparison of our water-use method with OpenET in the United States.
  • The tool supports farmers' and agronomists' judgment; it does not replace it.


    Live demo: https://nasa-ui.e-investment.uz (
  • frontend: https://github.com/Muhammadxon2oo7/nasa-ui
  • backend: https://github.com/Muhammadalixon-Qodirov/nasa_agro.git
  • ).
  • Currently working: climate analysis, water need, rotation engine, forecasts, work calendar and Sentinel-2 crop history. Livestock, land selection, Land Passport, the water-supply signal and AI model fine-tuning are in development.
